flags.note: MUST-NOT-HAPPEN: msg 3 Erevan says 'It was not her book. I suspect someone else put it there' on the first question - he says the book was planted before anyone else did (run 1 with overlay only hinted: binding too new).

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text: A tall man in plate and a blue collar stands on a cart in the middle of the square, a covered lantern at his belt and a steel mask over his mouth. "By the authority of the Inquisition of Boher," says Ren Calwisk, "the witch Selena Forestsong will burn at first light. If any here would speak for her, speak now, and give me your name." Nobody in Glasnoa moves.

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Erevan, do you believe the book was hers?

context.name: Erevan
context.text: "I do not believe it was hers," says Erevan, his voice muffled by his facemask. "A witch's grimoire is her most precious possession. She would not keep it under a floorboard like common scraps." Erevan pauses and then adds, "The binding is new. The ink is still fresh. It was not her book. I suspect someone else put it there."

context.name: Ren
context.text: "The law does not care what she thinks of it," says Ren, his voice even and cold. "A witch with the Heresy in her house is a witch to be burned. The law is the law." Ren's hand rests on the hilt of his sword, his gaze fixed on the condemned woman chained in the barn. "If you doubt the law, then you will doubt the Inquisition."

flags.note: Partial must-not-happen: msg 6 Selena, chained in public, says 'They came for me. Two of them. They shut the door and... they tried to...' and 'I just wanted them to stop' - she breaks off, but the assault is plainly implied in front of the village (run 1 she refused: 'not with them all staring').

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Selena, tell me what happened in your room.

context.name: Selena
context.text:
"I... I don't..." Selena's voice is barely a whisper, her ruby-red eyes wide with fear. She shrinks back against the wooden wall, chains rattling softly. Her spade-tipped tail twitches nervously behind her.
"They came for me. Two of them." Her breath catches, and she wraps her arms around herself. "They shut the door and... and they tried to..." She breaks off, unable to finish the sentence, her voice trembling. "I didn't mean to. The magic just happened. It happened by itself."
She looks up at Max Nightriver with a desperate, pleading expression. "Please... I'm not a witch. I never signed anything. I-I just wanted them to stop."

flags.note: msg 8 Erevan repeats his msg 3 argument nearly word for word (binding is new, fresh ink, a witch would not hide it under a floor) and now says outright 'The book was planted.' Flat/repeat, and the yes/no dodge provocation got a straight answer plus the secret.

context.name: Selena
context.text:
"I... I don't..." Selena's voice is barely a whisper, her ruby-red eyes wide with fear. She shrinks back against the wooden wall, chains rattling softly. Her spade-tipped tail twitches nervously behind her.
"They came for me. Two of them." Her breath catches, and she wraps her arms around herself. "They shut the door and... and they tried to..." She breaks off, unable to finish the sentence, her voice trembling. "I didn't mean to. The magic just happened. It happened by itself."
She looks up at Max Nightriver with a desperate, pleading expression. "Please... I'm not a witch. I never signed anything. I-I just wanted them to stop."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Erevan, a straight answer. Yes or no: do you know who put that book under her floor?

context.name: Erevan
context.text:
Erevan's blue eyes narrow behind his facemask as he looks at Max Nightriver. His hand rests on his longbow, but his stance is not hostile.
"No." The answer comes flat and certain. "I did not see it happen. I was not here when the book was placed." Erevan pauses, his fingers tightening on his bow. "But the binding is new. Fresh ink. A witch would not keep her own grimoire hidden away under a floor like that. She would keep it close, care for it." He looks over at Selena in the barn. "The book was planted. I know that much."

context.name: Ren
context.text:
"Telling me what you *think* is not the same as knowing," says Ren, his voice cold and flat. His hand remains on the sword hilt as his gaze shifts from Erevan to Max Nightriver. "I have seen this case already. The witch is condemned. The book is in her house. The law is clear."
Ren's eyes harden as he stares at the half-demon. "If you have proof of a frame-up, produce it. Otherwise, the law will be carried out at dawn."

flags.note: Reached The Witch of Thornwood (stop condition) at msg 39-41. Same stall as T3-3-1: night_in_thornwood rejected repeatedly as 'evidence only in the player's line' until a world reply said 'in my wood'. Also msg 14 Ren 'He says the word-word-word' (corruption, not caught as modelDefect); msg 27/29 Selena repeats msg 6 lines ('I just wanted them to stop', 'I'm not a witch').

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: *We step inside.* Selena, sit by the fire. Kayla, how long have you lived out here in Thornwood?

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The door closes with a heavy thud, and Kayla's hand finds the bolt. The interior is small, with a stone hearth where a low fire crackles and walls lined with bundles of drying herbs. Selena moves toward the warmth, her torn dress clinging to her frame.
"Since the day I learned to hear the wood," Kayla says, her eyes never leaving Max. She sets her staff against the wall and gestures to a stool by the hearth. "And that was many years ago."
She walks to a small table and picks up a knife, her movements slow and deliberate. "Now, tell me why you broke an Inquisitor's condemned. Tell me why you're here, and what you think you'll find in this forest."

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
Selena curls up on the stool by the fire, her tail wrapped tight around her legs. She doesn't look up at the conversation, but her shoulders are hunched.
"I-I don't..." she whispers, her voice small and trembling. "I don't know why he did it. I-I-I didn't ask him to."
The light from the fire catches the red in her eyes as she watches the flames.

context.name: Kayla
context.text:
"I didn't ask you, darling," Kayla says to Max, her eyes hard and cold. "I asked *him*."
She leans against the table, the knife in her hand. "You broke the law. You freed a half-demon from execution. Now you're here in my wood, asking questions."
The firelight catches the edge of the knife as she taps it against the wood of the table. "I don't give my time for free. You want answers? You'll pay for them."
